name: Communitarianism
summary: Communitarianism holds that people are shaped by the families, communities and traditions they belong to, so a good society balances individual rights with responsibilities and the common good. It criticises liberal individualism and unregulated markets for eroding community, and places civil society (family, schools, local groups) between the individual and the state. The responsive form of Amitai Etzioni and the 1990 Platform is pluralist and strongly democratic, combining a stress on family and moral education with a defence of free speech and equal dignity.
scope: Responsive communitarianism, as set out in the 1990 Responsive Communitarian Platform (s7) and Etzioni's Britannica article (s6), together with the academic communitarians (Sandel, Taylor, MacIntyre, Walzer) as the SEP (s1) and Britannica describe them. It excludes the authoritarian East Asian 'communitarianism' that Britannica names as a separate school, and the older utopian-socialist use of the word. Positions come only from these defining sources; where they are silent the answer is null.
